course_title: Topics in Hispanic Culture: 21st Latin American Literature
subject: SPAN
course_description: Upper-level research seminar with a strong writing component on topics related to the language, discourse, literature, and/or culture of the Hispanic world. Students may take multiple SPAN 485W courses provided that they focus on different topics.
course_notes: Topic - From the Margins: Women, Indigenous, and Afro-Latin American Voices in Contemporary Literature What is being written in Latin America today? Latin American literature is experiencing a period of remarkable transformation, with women writers, Indigenous and Afro-Latin American voices, and new literary movements reshaping the region¿s literary landscape. From environmental dystopias and new perspectives on history and memory to horror and experimental writing, contemporary Latin American literature offers unique ways of understanding the crises and transformations of our time. Through close reading and critical writing, students will explore how a new generation of writers is imagining Latin America and its place in the twenty-first-century world. PREREQUISITE: At least one foundational course (SPAN 300-318W) or permission from the instructor.
